title: Redwood security review - SSO/SCIM/RBAC
summary: 30-40 minute technical review covering SSO/SAML config, SCIM provisioning, RBAC/least-privilege model, audit log retention, and KMS/encryption options. Agreed to run SCIM test account, provide SAML metadata and a proposed RBAC matrix, and follow up with SOC2 evidence pack.
topics: SSO / SAML setup and metadata exchange
SCIM provisioning workflow and user sync cadence
RBAC roles, least-privilege model, and admin separation
Audit logs, retention, and export / SIEM integration
Data residency and private deployment options
next_steps: Redwood to send SAML metadata and sample IdP config (Arianna)
Customer to provide test IdP tenant details for SCIM pilot (Priya)
Redwood SE to share RBAC role matrix and least-privilege recommendations (Marcus)
Send SOC 2 + ISO evidence packet and audit logs documentation

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Arianna (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jordan (ClearHealth Head of Security), Priya (IT Ops), Evan (SRE)

Summary: quick kickoff, then deep dive into SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning. Lots of questions about RBAC, separation of duties, and KMS integration.

[00:00] Arianna: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Arianna from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with Marcus our SE, we wanted to run through your SSO/SCIM and RBAC needs and make sure we align on a pilot plan
[00:12] Jordan: hey, thanks, yes we wanted to focus on least-priv, onboarding via SCIM, and how auth ties into your audit logs and encryption, we have some regulatory retention requirements
[00:22] Marcus: great, quick disclaimer, i'll cover the technical flows, SAML metadata, SCIM sync, role mapping, and how audit logs are surfaced, any high level constraints we should know about?
[00:34] Priya: we use Okta as our IdP, we want SCIM to provision groups automatically and sync once per 15 minutes ideally, and we need RBAC so that only certain teams can see PII-sensitive prompts and logs
[00:48] Evan: also curious about service accounts, who can call the Redwood API from our infra, we want separation between infra engineers and app owners
[00:56] Marcus: okay, so with Okta we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning, the flow is: you upload your IdP metadata into Redwood, we give you our SP metadata, then SCIM tokens for provisioning, and you can scope group-to-role mappings
[01:12] Jordan: and the SAML assertions, what attributes do you need? email, name, groups?
[01:18] Marcus: primary are email and groups, we can also accept custom attributes if you want department or cost center; groups map to roles in the console
[01:26] Priya: any gotchas with Okta? We've had sync issues previously when group names changed
[01:31] Marcus: yeah group renames can cause a mismatch, recommended pattern is stable group identifier mapping in Okta; also we support deprovisioning on SCIM delete, and can soft-deactivate accounts if preferred
[01:44] Arianna: quick Q — for audit and compliance, Jordan, do you have a retention target? e.g., 1 year, 7 years?
[01:50] Jordan: for our particular workflows it's 3 years for audit trails, but some parts of the org want 7 years, we're trying to be explicit about what's mandatory
[01:58] Marcus: Redwood stores audit logs in an immutable store by default for hosted customers, retention is configurable per account. For Dedicated/Private we can route logs to your SIEM or to an S3 bucket under customer control
[02:10] Evan: can we push logs to Splunk?
[02:12] Marcus: yes, we have S3 export and direct syslog/HTTP integration patterns, we can provide a connector example for Splunk and also a sample IAM policy for the S3 bucket
[02:22] Priya: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys? we need CMEK for some datasets
[02:27] Marcus: yes we support KMS/HSM integration for Private and Dedicated, for Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key options via partner KMS, but there are different trust boundaries; i'll detail that in the doc
[02:38] Jordan: how about RBAC primitives, what roles exist out of the box? we need least-priv and admin separation
[02:45] Marcus: out of the box we have roles: Owner, Admin, Developer, Viewer, Auditor, plus custom roles. Owner has full config rights, Admin can manage projects and billing, Developer can deploy models/calls, Viewer can't see secret tokens, Auditor can read logs but not change config
[03:01] Jordan: can we restrict read access to outputs that contain PII? we need a policy that prevents some teams from viewing raw completions
[03:09] Marcus: we support field-level masking and redaction rules at the route level, plus per-role permission gating on viewing past transcripts; we can also integrate with a pre-send redaction webhook if you want automated scrubbing
[03:22] Priya: what's the model for service accounts vs user accounts? we want service accounts that can be scoped to a single service and have no console UI access
[03:30] Marcus: service accounts are separate principals with token-based auth; you can attach roles to service accounts and disable console login for them. Tokens rotate and we have built-in token expiry policies
[03:40] Arianna: any regulatory concerns for ClearHealth specifically? Jordan: we handle PHI in certain flows, so HIPAA controls matter; we need BAAs for hosted services
[03:51] Arianna: Redwood offers Private deployment for PHI and BAAs on enterprise contracts; for hosted we have SOC 2 Type II and can discuss options, we'll include the compliance packet
[04:05] Marcus: technical detail on SCIM: we support group push and user push with incremental syncs, scim endpoint supports PATCH for partial updates, and we'll share our SCIM attribute mapping table
[04:18] Evan: how do you handle conflicts? say user already exists in Redwood with different email
[04:23] Marcus: matching priority is: externalId if present, then email; we can configure matching rules in the tenant settings; recommended to have externalId set from Okta to avoid ambiguity
[04:34] Priya: latency — SCIM sync every 15 minutes is fine, but can we do more frequent for critical groups?
[04:39] Marcus: yes we can support shorter cadence for pilot but at scale we recommend 5-15 minutes depending on churn; for high-change groups we can also trigger a manual sync via API
[04:47] Jordan: about audit logs, are they tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody for some events
[04:52] Marcus: logs are write-once into an append-only store with SHA hashing per batch, we can provide hashing proofs and chain-of-custody export to your audit team, for Dedicated we can stream raw events to your SIEM for full control
[05:05] Arianna: question on SAML metadata exchange timeline — how quickly can you onboard once we provide metadata?
[05:10] Marcus: usually within 24-48 hours to configure SSO/SCIM and run test provisioning if we have the test tenant and service account, more if you need custom attribute mapping
[05:20] Jordan: about least-priv role matrix, what is Redwood's recommended baseline?
[05:24] Marcus: recommended baseline: restrict log-read and PII-read to Auditor role, restrict token creation to Admin/Owner only, Developers can deploy and call but cannot change tenant-level security settings, Owners manage billing and integrations
[05:36] Priya: can we create a custom role that only allows model inference but not access to historical transcripts?
[05:41] Marcus: yes custom roles can be built from primitives (call_model, view_transcript, manage_integrations...) you can compose them to meet that requirement
[05:49] Evan: is there an approval workflow for elevated privileges? we want a JIT (just-in-time) elevation for emergency access
[05:55] Marcus: we have an audit workflow integration with your IdP for JIT elevation via SCIM group push or via our API for temporary tokens, we can also integrate with your PAM solution for approval gates
[06:08] Jordan: encryption at rest — can we enforce CMEK for all storage including audit logs?
[06:13] Marcus: for Private and Dedicated yes, for hosted there's a managed KMS option and we can support BYOK depending on contract; we'll clarify limits in the doc
[06:22] Arianna: any data residency constraints? we have EU and US data policies
[06:26] Marcus: we can pin tenant data to specific regions for hosted accounts, and Private deployments natively keep data on-prem; we'll map region options in the follow-up doc
[06:35] Priya: token management — do you support short lived tokens and automatic rotation?
[06:40] Marcus: yes, token TTLs are configurable, and we support rotation via API and rotation hooks to your secret manager, we also support auditing of token usage per principal
[06:49] Arianna: pause — let's capture some clarifying Qs, Jordan you mentioned 3 years retention, we should confirm which events need 3 years (admin, access, model calls)
[06:58] Jordan: correct, admin changes and access events 3 years, model call logs 1 year unless PII flagged then 3 years
[07:08] Marcus: we can tag events with classification and apply tiered retention, automatic purge for non-PII after 1 year and move PII to long-term storage with CMEK for 3 years
[07:18] Priya: about sharing SAML metadata, what's the recommended minimum attribute set?
[07:22] Marcus: email, externalId, groups, displayName; costCenter if you want to do billing segmentation
[07:31] Evan: do you have a sandbox tenant we can use to test SCIM and RBAC without touching prod?
[07:35] Arianna: yes we can provision a trial sandbox, we'll include a separate sandbox tenant for the pilot with separate logs and sandbox keys
[07:44] Marcus: also re: SCIM rate limits, we'll give you a recommended rate for group pushes, but for initial bulk sync we have a one-time import endpoint to avoid rate throttling
[07:56] Jordan: legal/BAA — what's the process for signing a BAA for PHI?
[07:59] Arianna: our legal can start the BAA once we move to an enterprise contract; Private deployments include BAAs more commonly, we'll connect legal post-call
[08:08] Priya: small nit — can we restrict who can request RBAC role changes? need an approval flow
[08:13] Marcus: yes approval flows are supported via integration with your ticketing system or via IdP group membership change that requires approval
[08:21] Arianna: ok time check, we have about 40 minutes left, let's go through a quick demo of where SAML metadata is uploaded in the console and how role mapping looks
[08:30] Marcus: demo: console -> settings -> SSO, here's SP metadata, click 'Download' and upload to Okta, the mapping UI shows left side IdP groups and right side Redwood roles, you can create a mapping rule with regex
[08:50] Jordan: that mapping UI looks helpful, can we export the mappings as JSON?
[08:55] Marcus: yes you can export/import mappings as JSON for reproducible config, handy for infra-as-code
[09:04] Evan: audit logs — can we filter by user, action, and model id?
[09:10] Marcus: yes filters include user, action, route, model id, request id, and timestamp range, and you can pin queries and schedule exports to S3 for long-term retention
[09:20] Priya: can we prove deletion? like if we purge a user, how do we prove the log shows deletion event?
[09:25] Marcus: deletion events are recorded with before/after payloads and retention markers, and we log the operator principal for the delete so chain-of-custody is preserved
[09:35] Jordan: SCIM pilot — what does success look like?
[09:39] Arianna: success criteria: automatic provisioning of 50 pilot users, correct group-to-role mapping, deprovision flows validated, and audit events appear in SIEM within 5 minutes
[09:49] Marcus: for the pilot we recommend a small subset of users and one service account to validate token scoping and log export, we'll run a checklist during the POC kickoff
[09:59] Priya: timeline — we want pilot next 2 weeks if possible
[10:03] Arianna: we can aim for pilot start in two weeks, assuming Priya can share test IdP by next week and we deliver metadata and RBAC matrix within 48 hours
[10:12] Jordan: any security hardening guidance for initial onboarding? e.g., restrict ports, IP allowlists?
[10:18] Marcus: yes we support IP allowlists per project, tenant-level mTLS for Dedicated, and network policies for Private; we'll include example firewall rules and minimum TLS versions supported
[10:30] Evan: are there any limitations around headers or custom claims in SAML assertions?
[10:34] Marcus: we accept standard claims and can map custom claims via the mapping UI, but very large payloads may be truncated, recommend using attributes not huge blobs
[10:44] Arianna: quick commercial note — dedicated/private pricing and data egress, we'll scope after technical fit, but we can share a draft SOW after pilot
[10:53] Jordan: ok sounds good, last Q on access logs, can we get a daily digest of failed auth attempts?
[10:58] Marcus: yes scheduled reports are supported, you can schedule daily/weekly digests and we can push to email or S3/HTTP endpoint
[11:06] Priya: thanks, this was helpful, we'll get the test tenant details and confirm retention requirements
[11:10] Arianna: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the SAML/SCIM docs and the RBAC matrix, Marcus will attach the technical notes and SCIM attribute mapping, Jordan we'll loop legal for BAA next steps
[11:22] Jordan: thanks all, talk soon

End transcript.
